ui.presetCustom: The options are set by hand.

reliable.name: Reliable
reliable.hint: Closer to real x86: slower, but fewer crashes and oddities.

fast.name: Fast
fast.hint: Bigger translation blocks and an unshrunk cache: faster in heavy scenes, more memory.

crash.fex-tso: If the game crashes at random places. It will run slower.
crash.fex-x87: If it crashes in scenes with physics or the camera shakes.
crash.fex-smc: For games with copy protection, or made with .NET or Unity.

memory.d3d9-maxAvailableMemory: A DirectX 9 game keeps fewer textures at once.
memory.dxvk-maxMemoryBudget: DXVK takes less memory; textures may load in late.
memory.fex-maxinst: Less memory for the game's translated code.

threads.dxvk-numCompilerThreads: Leaves more tasks to the game itself. New effects take longer to appear.

input-mode.name: Control mode
input-mode.hint: Controller: the game sees an Xbox 360 gamepad. Keyboard and mouse: Switch buttons press keys.

left-deadzone.name: Left stick dead zone
left-deadzone.hint: How much stick travel is not counted as a tilt: hides Joy-Con drift.

right-deadzone.name: Right stick dead zone
right-deadzone.hint: The same for the right stick.

keyboard-auto.name: On-screen keyboard by itself
keyboard-auto.hint: Shows up when the game waits for text.

frame-limit.name: Frame limit
frame-limit.hint: Keeps the game from drawing faster than this: smoother frames, less heat and battery drain.

vsync.name: Vertical sync
vsync.hint: Frames change together with the screen refresh — no tearing. Off can be faster.

upscaling.name: Scaling
upscaling.hint: How the picture is enlarged when the game draws less than 1280×720. Integer is for pixel art.

upscaling-sharpness.name: FSR sharpness
upscaling-sharpness.hint: If small text has a bright halo, lower it.

dxvk-hud.name: DXVK counter
dxvk-hud.hint: Frame rate and DXVK details over the game, to judge speed.

lsfg.name: LSFG-VK frame generation
lsfg.hint: Inserts a drawn frame between the game's frames: smoother, but controls lag a little. Needs Lossless.dll.

lsfg-performance.name: Performance mode
lsfg-performance.hint: Faster, but the in-between frames are less accurate.

lsfg-flow.name: Optical flow scale
lsfg-flow.hint: Resolution used to find motion: lower is faster, higher is more accurate.

dxvk-maxMemoryBudget.name: DXVK memory budget
dxvk-maxMemoryBudget.hint: How much memory DXVK takes for textures and buffers. Lower runs out less often, but textures may load in late.

dxgi-maxDeviceMemory.name: Video memory for the game (DX10–12)
dxgi-maxDeviceMemory.hint: How much video memory the game sees. Lower it if the game fills memory and crashes; it adds no real memory.

dxgi-maxSharedMemory.name: Shared memory for the game (DX10–12)
dxgi-maxSharedMemory.hint: How much shared memory the game is told about. Reserves nothing.

d3d9-maxAvailableMemory.name: Video memory for the game (DX9)
d3d9-maxAvailableMemory.hint: How much free video memory a DirectX 9 game sees. Lower keeps fewer textures and runs out less often.

d3d9-textureMemory.name: Texture upload buffer (DX9)
d3d9-textureMemory.hint: Lower saves memory, but textures load with hitches.

dxvk-enableMemoryDefrag.name: Video memory defragmenting
dxvk-enableMemoryDefrag.hint: Gathers scattered pieces of memory so it lasts longer.

dxvk-trackPipelineLifetime.name: Free unused shaders
dxvk-trackPipelineLifetime.hint: Drops compiled shaders from memory sooner: saves memory, but sometimes compiles again.

dxgi-maxFrameLatency.name: Frame queue (DX10–12)
dxgi-maxFrameLatency.hint: How many frames are prepared ahead. Fewer makes controls snappier, but the frame rate can drop.

d3d9-maxFrameLatency.name: Frame queue (DX9)
d3d9-maxFrameLatency.hint: How many frames are prepared ahead. Fewer makes controls snappier, but the frame rate can drop.

dxvk-latencySleep.name: Latency reduction
dxvk-latencySleep.hint: DXVK waits before a frame so input reaches it fresh. Lowers the frame rate in some games.

dxvk-tearFree.name: Tear-free
dxvk-tearFree.hint: On: no tearing even without VSync. Off: allows tearing when a frame is late.

dxvk-numCompilerThreads.name: Shader compiler threads
dxvk-numCompilerThreads.hint: Fewer leaves more CPU and tasks to the game, but new effects take longer to appear.

dxvk-enableGraphicsPipelineLibrary.name: Fast shader assembly (GPL)
dxvk-enableGraphicsPipelineLibrary.hint: Shaders are built from ready parts: fewer stutters the first time an effect shows. Turn off if something draws wrong.

d3d9-floatEmulation.name: Shader math accuracy (DX9)
d3d9-floatEmulation.hint: How DirectX 9 math is reproduced. Try it for wrong lighting or black objects.

dxvk-lowerSinCos.name: Own sine and cosine
dxvk-lowerSinCos.hint: Its own formula instead of the driver's. Helps when water, shadows or animation shake.

d3d9-useFP16.name: Half precision (DX9)
d3d9-useFP16.hint: Shaders count in 16 bits where they may: faster, but banding and colour errors are possible.

d3d11-maxTessFactor.name: Tessellation limit (DX11)
d3d11-maxTessFactor.hint: Lower makes the GPU faster but surfaces simpler.

d3d11-disableMsaa.name: Turn off MSAA (DX11)
d3d11-disableMsaa.hint: Saves GPU work and memory; edges get jagged.

d3d11-samplerAnisotropy.name: Anisotropic filtering (DX10–11)
d3d11-samplerAnisotropy.hint: Sharper textures at an angle — roads, floors. Costs GPU time.

d3d9-samplerAnisotropy.name: Anisotropic filtering (DX8–9)
d3d9-samplerAnisotropy.hint: Sharper textures at an angle — roads, floors. Costs GPU time.

d3d11-samplerLodBias.name: Texture detail (DX11)
d3d11-samplerLodBias.hint: Plus is blurrier but faster; minus is sharper but may shimmer.

d3d9-samplerLodBias.name: Texture detail (DX9)
d3d9-samplerLodBias.hint: Plus is blurrier but faster; minus is sharper but may shimmer.

d3d11-clampNegativeLodBias.name: Remove texture shimmer (DX11)
d3d11-clampNegativeLodBias.hint: Keeps the game from over-sharpening textures — less shimmer.

d3d9-clampNegativeLodBias.name: Remove texture shimmer (DX9)
d3d9-clampNegativeLodBias.hint: Keeps the game from over-sharpening textures — less shimmer.

dxgi-deferSurfaceCreation.name: Late window creation (DX10–12)
dxgi-deferSurfaceCreation.hint: For games that crash or go black at start while switching how they draw.

d3d9-deferSurfaceCreation.name: Late window creation (DX9)
d3d9-deferSurfaceCreation.hint: For games that crash or go black at start while switching how they draw.

d3d9-forceAspectRatio.name: Only one aspect ratio (DX9)
d3d9-forceAspectRatio.hint: The game sees only screen modes of this ratio — less confusion with a stretched picture.

dxgi-forceRefreshRate.name: Refresh rate for the game (DX10–12)
dxgi-forceRefreshRate.hint: Which refresh rate the game sees. The Switch screen does not change.

d3d9-forceRefreshRate.name: Refresh rate for the game (DX9)
d3d9-forceRefreshRate.hint: Which refresh rate the game sees. The Switch screen does not change.

d3d9-modeCountCompatibility.name: Short list of resolutions (DX9)
d3d9-modeCountCompatibility.hint: For old games that crash on a long list of screen modes.

d3d11-cachedDynamicResources.name: Cached buffers (DX11)
d3d11-cachedDynamicResources.hint: For games that often read data back from video memory and slow down from it.

d3d9-deviceLocalConstantBuffers.name: Shader constants in video memory (DX9)
d3d9-deviceLocalConstantBuffers.hint: The Switch shares its memory, so this is not always faster — check it.

d3d9-cachedWriteOnlyBuffers.name: Cached buffers (DX9)
d3d9-cachedWriteOnlyBuffers.hint: For games that read from write-only buffers and slow down badly from it.

d3d9-allowDirectBufferMapping.name: Direct buffer access (DX9)
d3d9-allowDirectBufferMapping.hint: Turn off if the game flickers or garbles geometry.

d3d11-disableDirectImageMapping.name: Texture workaround (DX11)
d3d11-disableDirectImageMapping.hint: For games whose textures and videos come out skewed or distorted.

d3d11-enableContextLock.name: Race protection (DX11)
d3d11-enableContextLock.hint: For games that crash from drawing on several threads at once; a little slower.

d3d11-exposeDriverCommandLists.name: Multithreaded drawing (DX11)
d3d11-exposeDriverCommandLists.hint: The game uses this to choose whether to draw on several threads. Turn off if it crashes or stutters.

d3d11-forceComputeLdsBarriers.name: Compute shader barriers (DX11)
d3d11-forceComputeLdsBarriers.hint: Against flicker and garbage in effects — lighting, particles; a little slower.

d3d11-forceComputeUavBarriers.name: Extra UAV barriers (DX11)
d3d11-forceComputeUavBarriers.hint: The same with another kind of barrier.

d3d9-lenientClear.name: Fast frame clear (DX9)
d3d9-lenientClear.hint: Can be faster, but sometimes clears too much at the edges.

d3d9-forceSamplerTypeSpecConstants.name: Texture type fix (DX9)
d3d9-forceSamplerTypeSpecConstants.hint: For games with black or missing textures.

dxvk-enableDescriptorBuffer.name: Descriptor buffers
dxvk-enableDescriptorBuffer.hint: Another way to hand textures to shaders. Turn off if textures vanish or the game crashes.

dxvk-enableDescriptorHeap.name: Descriptor heaps
dxvk-enableDescriptorHeap.hint: The same, the newer way; it wins over descriptor buffers.

dxvk-enableUnifiedImageLayouts.name: Unified image layouts
dxvk-enableUnifiedImageLayouts.hint: Turn off only to look for the cause of garbage on screen.

dxvk-enableImplicitResolves.name: Implicit MSAA resolves
dxvk-enableImplicitResolves.hint: Do not turn off without a reason: stripes appear on the Switch's GPU.

dxvk-useRawSsbo.name: Raw shader buffer access
dxvk-useRawSsbo.hint: For debugging only: forcing it can break drawing.

d3d11-maxFeatureLevel.name: DirectX feature level (DX11)
d3d11-maxFeatureLevel.hint: The game thinks the GPU is older: it may choose a simpler mode or avoid a failing new one.

dxgi-hideNvidiaGpu.name: Hide NVIDIA (DX10–12)
dxgi-hideNvidiaGpu.hint: The game does not recognize the NVIDIA GPU and skips the special paths for it it may crash on.

dxgi-hideNvkGpu.name: Hide the NVK driver (DX10–12)
dxgi-hideNvkGpu.hint: The game does not see that the driver is NVK.

d3d9-hideNvidiaGpu.name: Hide NVIDIA (DX9)
d3d9-hideNvidiaGpu.hint: The game does not recognize the NVIDIA GPU and skips the special paths for it.

d3d9-hideNvkGpu.name: Hide the NVK driver (DX9)
d3d9-hideNvkGpu.hint: The game does not see that the driver is NVK.

fex-tso.name: Strict memory ordering
fex-tso.hint: Orders memory access as x86 does. Slower; turn it on when a multithreaded game crashes, hangs or corrupts data.

fex-x87-single.name: x87 in single precision
fex-x87-single.hint: Computes x87 float math at the precision Direct3D 9 sets, without extra conversions. Faster. Turn off if numbers, physics or the picture look wrong.

fex-gdb-symbols.name: Exact code map for the profiler
fex-gdb-symbols.hint: The profiler sees every instruction of the game, not only some. For measurements only; no effect on speed.

fex-call-cache.name: Remembered targets of indirect calls
fex-call-cache.hint: Each call whose target is known only at run time remembers where it went the first time, and later calls to the same place skip the lookup. Turn off if the game crashes, hangs or runs slower.

fex-jump-tables.name: Direct jumps for switches
fex-jump-tables.hint: A choice between many branches in the game's code (a switch) goes straight to the right branch instead of searching for it each time. Turn off if the game crashes, hangs or runs slower.

fex-compact-returns.name: Compact returns
fex-compact-returns.hint: When a function returns, the rarely needed search for where to go back is kept away from the main code, so more of the game's code fits the processor's fast cache. Turn off if the game crashes, hangs or runs slower.

fex-slim-return-points.name: Lighter returns from functions
fex-slim-return-points.hint: Coming back from a function no longer records which piece of translated code is running; if something goes wrong, it is worked out on the spot. Less work on every return. Turn off if the game crashes, hangs or runs slower.

large-pages.name: Large memory pages
large-pages.hint: Big blocks of the game's memory are placed so the console can map them in large pieces, and the processor finds its data faster. Turn off if the game crashes, hangs, runs out of memory or runs slower.

orchestrator.name: Orchestrator
orchestrator.hint: Watches how busy each of the game's threads is. When one thread does most of the work, it gets a core of its own and everything else moves off it. Turn off if the game stutters or runs slower.

d3d9-front-end-thread.name: Graphics on its own thread (DX9)
d3d9-front-end-thread.hint: Direct3D 9 work moves to a thread on a free core, so the game's own thread has less to do. Turn off if the picture breaks, the game hangs or runs slower.

d3d9-effect-thread.name: Game effects on their own thread (DX9)
d3d9-effect-thread.hint: The game's built-in shader effect code moves to another free core, next to the graphics thread. Works only together with “Graphics on its own thread”. Turn off if the picture breaks, the game hangs or runs slower.

d3d9-effect-pass-merge.name: Game effects without repeats (DX9)
d3d9-effect-pass-merge.hint: The game effects thread does less: when the game draws many objects with the same effect, only what changed between them is sent again. Works only together with “Game effects on their own thread”. Turn off if the picture breaks, the game hangs or runs slower.

d3d9-managed-buffer-copies.name: Model data without waiting (DX9)
d3d9-managed-buffer-copies.hint: When the game changes the data of its models, it no longer waits for the graphics thread to catch up: the change goes into the queue with everything else. Uses a little more memory. Works only together with “Graphics on its own thread”. Turn off if the picture breaks, the game hangs or runs slower.

fex-x87.name: Reduced x87 precision
fex-x87.hint: Old x87 math in 64 bits instead of 80 — much faster. Turn off if the camera shakes, physics act up or objects vanish.

fex-smc.name: Self-modifying code checks
fex-smc.hint: Needed by games with protection, a packer, .NET, Mono or LuaJIT. MTrack is the normal mode; Full is very slow.

fex-maxinst.name: Translation block size
fex-maxinst.hint: How many game instructions are translated at once. More is faster in heavy scenes; fewer saves memory and shortens stutters.

fex-multiblock.name: Large code blocks
fex-multiblock.hint: Translates connected pieces of code together: usually faster, but translating takes longer and more memory.

fex-l2.name: Second jump cache (L2)
fex-l2.hint: An extra table of jumps between code blocks. May remove small stutters, but takes memory.

fex-l1.name: Jump cache sizing (L1)
fex-l1.hint: Shrinks each thread's jump cache to save memory. Off may be faster, at up to 1 MB a thread.

fex-vector-tso.name: TSO for vector operations
fex-vector-tso.hint: Only with strict memory ordering: extends it to SSE operations. Safer, but slower still.

fex-memcpy-tso.name: TSO for memory copies
fex-memcpy-tso.hint: Only with strict memory ordering: strict ordering for bulk copies too.

fex-half-barrier.name: Light TSO barriers
fex-half-barrier.hint: Only with strict memory ordering: unaligned accesses get cheaper barriers.

fex-split-locks.name: Strict atomics across lines
fex-split-locks.hint: An atomic operation across cache lines does not tear. Against rare hangs of multithreaded games; slower.

fex-unaligned.name: Fix unaligned atomics
fex-unaligned.hint: After the first fault FEX rewrites the operation so it does not fault again. Turning it off usually only slows down.

fex-volatile.name: Hints from the exe file
fex-volatile.hint: Where the exe marks strict ordering as unneeded, FEX skips it — faster. Turn off if the game is unstable.

fex-mono.name: Mono and Unity mode
fex-mono.hint: Special handling for Mono games: smaller blocks and rewritten code taken into account. No effect on other games.

fex-hypervisor.name: Hide virtualization
fex-hypervisor.hint: The game does not see a virtual machine. For games and protections that refuse to run in one.

fex-small-tsc.name: Time counter scaling
fex-small-tsc.hint: The Switch's slow timer is scaled to the rate x86 programs expect. Change it if the game runs at the wrong speed.

fex-hybrid.name: Hide mixed cores
fex-hybrid.hint: The game sees every core as the same. Usually keep it on.

fex-l1-increase.name: L1 cache growth threshold
fex-l1-increase.hint: Lower grows the jump cache more readily: faster, more memory. Only with jump cache sizing.

fex-l1-decrease.name: L1 cache shrink threshold
fex-l1-decrease.hint: Higher gives memory back more readily: thriftier, more misses. Only with jump cache sizing.

windows.name: Window output
windows.hint: Framebuffer is the fallback when the game's windows show wrong.

verbose.name: Verbose log
verbose.hint: Wine's detailed log. Slows the game a lot — only for finding bugs.

profile.name: Profiler
profile.hint: Writes where the game spends its time into the log. Slows the start.

library.selectHint: Select a game to install it on the Switch, rebuild or delete it.

card.runtimeOutdated: Built with runtime {{version}}; Carafe has a newer one. Rebuild the game to get the fixes.
card.installedSd: Done: the game is installed on the Switch SD card.
card.installedNand: Done: the game is installed in console memory.
card.logsSaved: Logs copied to {{path}}, the folder is open.

card.deleteConfirm: Delete the “{{title}}” NSP from this PC? The game stays on the console.

errors.io: Could not read or write a file.
errors.pack: Packing failed — see the build log for details.
errors.blocked: Your antivirus blocked runtime files in the .carafe service folder inside the library — the build log lists them. These are Wine DLLs from the Autorun repository: Carafe verified their checksums before the build, and antivirus heuristics sometimes mistake them for a threat. Add the .carafe folder to the exclusions (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → Exclusions) and build again.
errors.noSpace: There is not enough space for the build on the drive with the library folder — the build log shows how much is needed and how much is free. While a game is being built, it takes up about four times the size of the finished NSP together with the Carafe runtime. Free up space on the drive or choose a library folder on another drive in Settings.
errors.pathTooLong: The path to one of the game files in the build folder is longer than the hacBrewPack packer can read — the build log shows the longest path and the limit. Non-Latin letters count as two or three characters. Shorten the path: move the library folder closer to the root of the drive (in Settings) or give the game folder a shorter name — its name is part of the path too.
errors.runtimeDamaged: Carafe runtime files are missing, unreadable or changed — the build log lists them. Most often this is the antivirus: its heuristics sometimes mistake Wine DLLs from the Autorun repository for a threat and quarantine them. Restore the files from quarantine (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Protection history) or reinstall Carafe, add the Carafe folder to the exclusions and build again.
errors.device: The Switch is not responding. Check that DBI is open in MTP mode.
errors.network: The website is not responding. Check your internet connection and try again.
errors.apiKey: The SteamGridDB API key is missing or was rejected — check it in the settings.
errors.unsupported: This file is not an image Carafe can read.
errors.icon: Could not make the icon — see the build log for details.
errors.invalid: The data did not pass validation.
errors.busy: A build or a USB install is running — wait for it to finish.
errors.cancelled: The build is cancelled, and its unfinished files are removed.

onboarding.welcomeText: Carafe turns a Windows game into a Switch app.
onboarding.keysText: A Switch app is encrypted with your console’s keys. They live in a prod.keys file that you dump from the console once with Lockpick_RCM:
onboarding.keysStep1: Reboot into Hekate, open Payloads and launch Lockpick_RCM.
onboarding.keysStep2: Choose Dump from sysNAND — the keys are saved to switch/prod.keys on the microSD card.
onboarding.keysStep3: Move the file to your PC: in Hekate, Tools → USB Tools → SD Card, or take the card out.
onboarding.keysNoLockpick: CFW packs usually include Lockpick_RCM. If it isn’t under Payloads, put Lockpick_RCM.bin into bootloader/payloads on the microSD card.
onboarding.keysOk: Required keys found: header_key and key_area_key_application_00.
onboarding.keysPrivacy: Carafe reads the keys only while packing and never copies them.
onboarding.libraryText: Carafe puts finished NSPs here. Each file keeps its own settings, so the folder can move to another computer.
onboarding.noticeSource: Games run through Autorun, an open-source project that brings Wine to the Switch. Carafe uses its prebuilt files and checks them before every build.
onboarding.noticeDefender: Windows Defender sometimes flags individual Wine DLLs. If a file goes missing, Carafe stops the build and shows how to add an exclusion.
onboarding.noticeWarranty: Carafe is free, open-source software. It comes as is, with no warranty, and you use it at your own risk.

wizard.waitLoading: Wait for the loading to finish
wizard.folderMissing: The game folder is no longer where it was — point to its new location.

folder.installedHint: Carafe needs an installed game, not an installer. If you only have setup.exe, install the game on this PC first.

launch.archHintAuto: {{file}} is {{arch}}. Change it only if the game doesn’t start.

launch.archWasReset: Bitness is back to Auto ({{arch}}) for the new file.

warnings.unstableX64: 64-bit games are not stable yet. If the game has a 32-bit version, use that.
warnings.steamApi: The folder has steam_api.dll: the game may need the Steam client and then won’t start. GOG versions usually work.
warnings.installerSelected: This looks like an installer or uninstaller, not the game itself.
warnings.onlyInstallers: The folder only has installers. Install the game on this PC and pick its folder.
warnings.x86OnX64: This is a 64-bit program: it won’t start in 32-bit memory.
warnings.x64OnFixedAddress: This older game needs its own address in memory, and 64-bit memory doesn’t have it. The game will most likely close right after it starts.

look.versionHint: Leave empty to use the build number ({{version}}).

art.noImages: This game has no square covers.

art.keyRejected: SteamGridDB rejected the key. Check it or create a new one.

art.keyStep3: Paste the key here and press Save.

input.modeKeyboardHint: Switch buttons press keys and mouse buttons. Suits most older games.
input.modeControllerHint: The game sees an Xbox 360 controller. Suits games with gamepad support.
input.deadzoneHint: The part of stick travel that doesn’t count as a tilt: it hides Joy-Con drift. Stick feels sluggish — lower it to 0–2; character creeps on its own — raise it.
input.keyboardAutoHint: Appears when the game waits for text input.

controls.pressOrPick: Press a key or a combination — or pick a mouse action:

graphics.frameLimitHint: Keeps the game from drawing faster than this: smoother frames, less heat and battery drain. The Switch screen runs at 60 Hz. Applies to Vulkan, DXVK and VKD3D.
graphics.hudHint: Frame rate and DXVK details over the game, to judge speed. It also changes how DXVK draws, so keep it off for playing.

upscalingHints.off: Stretches the picture to the screen with a slight blur.
upscalingHints.fsr: AMD FSR 1.0: stretches more crisply and adds sharpening. Good for old low-resolution games.
upscalingHints.integer: Every pixel becomes an even square — for pixel art. Only pictures up to 640×360 get enlarged; otherwise you get black borders.

graphics.upscalingScope: Works when the game draws below 1280×720 through Vulkan, DXVK or VKD3D.
graphics.sharpnessHint: Lower it if small text gets a bright halo.
graphics.vsyncHint: Frames change together with the screen refresh — no tearing. Off can be faster but tears. Overrides the game’s own setting; applies to Vulkan, DXVK and VKD3D.
graphics.lsfgHint: Inserts a generated frame between game frames: smoother, with slightly delayed controls. Needs Lossless.dll from your own copy of Lossless Scaling — a Carafe NSP can’t carry it yet, so this setting does nothing for now.
graphics.lsfgPerformanceHint: Faster, with less accurate in-between frames.
graphics.lsfgFlowHint: Resolution used to find motion: lower is faster, higher is more accurate.

advanced.title: Advanced

windowsHints.auto: The compositor assembles the game’s windows — Carafe’s loading screen and cursor rely on it.
windowsHints.framebuffer: Windows are copied straight to the screen, without the compositor. A fallback if windows show up wrong; Carafe’s loading screen and cursor may not work.

advanced.verboseHint: A detailed Wine log in a separate file. Slows the game down a lot — only for hunting bugs.
advanced.profileHint: Logs where the game spends time. Slows the start down.

settings.title: Settings
settings.keysIncomplete: This file lacks the required keys — builds will fail.
settings.steamGridDbHint: Needed to search for covers. Get it at steamgriddb.com → sign in → Preferences → API.
settings.defaultsHint: The wizard starts from these. Games already built stay as they are.
settings.resetConfirm: Restore the recommended settings for new games? Controls, button layout and graphics will become what Carafe recommends for the Switch. Games already built won’t change.

updatesHint.automatic: Twice a day Carafe looks at its releases page on GitHub and downloads a new version in the background. It installs only when you ask. The check sends nothing else.
updatesHint.notifyOnly: Twice a day Carafe looks at its releases page on GitHub and shows a button in the library. It downloads only when you ask.
updatesHint.off: Carafe doesn’t contact GitHub on its own. Check with the button below.

update.title: Carafe update
update.runtimeChanged: The runtime is updated: afterwards, rebuild your games to give them the fixes.
update.downloadingHint: Keep working as usual. When it’s downloaded, this button offers a restart.
update.readyHint: Your library, settings and built games stay as they are. The restart takes a few seconds.
update.onCloseSet: The update installs when you close Carafe.
update.busyHint: A build or a USB install is running — restarting now would interrupt it.

download.title: The update didn’t download
download.text: The download stopped. Nothing in Carafe has changed.

verify.title: The update failed the check
verify.text: The downloaded file isn’t signed for this release, so Carafe won’t install it. Nothing in Carafe has changed.

install.title: The update didn’t install
install.text: The installer didn’t finish, and Carafe is still on {{version}}. Your library and settings are untouched.

update.found: Carafe {{version}} is out — see the button in the library
update.devBuild: This development build doesn’t update itself.

rebuild.offerTitle_one: {{count}} game is built with an older runtime
rebuild.offerTitle_other: {{count}} games are built with an older runtime
rebuild.offerText: Rebuilding gives them the fixes of runtime {{version}}.
rebuild.title: Rebuild with runtime {{version}}
rebuild.intro: Games are built one by one with the same settings, Title ID and icon. The old NSP is replaced only after a successful build.
rebuild.nothing: Every game is built with the current runtime. Nothing to rebuild.
rebuild.space: Needs up to {{size}} of free space on the library drive
rebuild.reinstallHint: Install each rebuilt game on the Switch again. Your saves on the console stay: the Title ID is the same.

registry.lead: Entries Carafe puts into this game's Windows registry. The menu rows below appear on the Switch in System › Game registry as ordinary settings with a list of values. The game's whole registry can be viewed and changed there too.

modeHints.once: At the first start and after a new build. What the game or you change later stays.
modeHints.everyStart: The entries come back at every start, even if the game changed them.

registry.emptyText: Import a .reg file — from the game's guide, say, or exported from the registry on a PC — or add an entry by hand.
registry.name: Name
registry.nameHint: An empty name is the default value (@).

valueHints.expandString: Text where %VARIABLES% are filled in when it is read.
valueHints.dword: A decimal number or 0x… — from 0 to 4294967295.
valueHints.qword: A decimal number or 0x… — up to 18446744073709551615.
valueHints.binary: Bytes in hexadecimal: de ad be ef.
valueHints.deleteValue: The value is removed from the key.
valueHints.deleteKey: The key is removed with everything in it.

invalid.dword: A number from 0 to 4294967295 or 0x… is needed.
invalid.qword: A number up to 18446744073709551615 or 0x… is needed.

registry.menuText: Each row changes one or several entries at once
registry.importText: Tick what goes into the game. HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT becomes HKLM\Software\Classes and Wow6432Node is dropped: the game has one registry for 32 and 64 bits. Deletions come along too.

skipReasons.unknownRoot: the game's registry has no such root
skipReasons.noKey: a value before the first key

importErrors.format: This is not a Windows registry file: its first line must be “Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00” or “REGEDIT4”.

registry.preview: How it looks on the Switch
registry.noRows: No menu rows yet. Pick an entry in the table and press “Make a menu row”, or add a row on the left.
